content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors present two main contributions. Firstly, they propose MAE+ baseline, which brings multi-crop tokenization to MAE and Masked Image Modeling (MIM). Their baseline, MAE+, randomly crops images by half, reducing the computing complexity by a factor of 16. MAE+ offers a good trade-off between compute resources and accuracy on ImageNet1K. Their best MAE+ setup outperforms regular MAE by 0.3% and 0.1% with ViT-B and ViT-L backbones, respectively.
Their second contribution is adversarial learning of perturbations applied to the positional encoding of image tokens. The authors propose Embedding and Coordinate mode adversaries. Embedding mode perturbs the token embeddings, while the Coordinate mode perturbs coordinates directly. They apply both strategies to absolute and relative positional embeddings. Their approach, named AdPE, outperforms MAE by 0.8% and 0.4% accuracy on ImageNet1K. In addition, it outperforms MAE in transfer learning tasks with ViT-B backbone by 2.6% and 3.2% on ADE20K and COCO, respectively.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. Their methods integrate seamlessly with MAE.
2. They performed extensive experiments with nice visualizations.
3. Good ablations on Absolute vs Relative positional embeddings were reported.
4. Nice and Clear explanation of their methods, particularly sections 3 and 4.

Weakness:
1. They use MAE+ (4k) for their experiments which use 100 hours of GPU more than MAE. What would be the performance of MAE if it was allowed the same amount of computational resources?
2. In Figure 1, MAE+ (2k) was not trained to 1600 epochs. 
3. The authors mention feeding all the tokens (masked and unmasked) to the encoder of MAE+. They do not report any ablation results of feeding only unmasked tokens.
4. What is the extra computational resources needed to run AdPE compared to MAE+? (the cost of using adversarial perturbations)
5. It is unclear what are the reasons for the performance gain of AdPE because the authors did not run the adversarial perturbation on top of regular MAE; they just used MAE+. Can you provide the results of using regular MAE with the adversarial perturbation?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The methodology and paper writing are clear.
Reproducibility: The authors provide an open-access repository to reproduce their results. 
Novelty: The idea of using adversarial perturbations to positional encodings in a Masked Image Modeling setup is novel.
content.summary_of_the_review: The use of adversarial perturbations to positional encodings leads to better results. The approach is simple and can seamlessly integrate with MAE. There are some concerns related to the computational resources needed. Nonetheless, the work is promising.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents an adversarial positional embedding approach for unsupervised learning of vision transformers. It considers using locally correlated patches and also uses both absolute and relative positional encodings for feature embeddings. The experimental results show favorable improvements over the baseline model.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
+ The usage of both relative and absolute positional encoding seems to be interesting

Cons:
- The technical novelty is not sufficient, and the overall performances compared to the state-of-the-arts are quite minor. 
- The paper could be presented better. The motivation for the different designs is not well explained, and the experimental results do not fully support the proposed designs.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work improves pretraining vision transformers by adversarial positional embedding. This prevents the transformer learning trivial features from the pretext task, thus improves the unsupervised learning of the transformers. This work also proposes a new baseline that show stronger performance on several datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
+ The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the competing methods.
+ A good extension for the transformer to learn adversarial positional embeddings.
Weaknesses
+ In Table 1, the improvements in ACC from the proposed method are marginal. In addition, it is unclear whether the proposed method performs well on other large-scale datasets.
+ This work proposes to perform adversarial perturbations in the embedding space and spatial coordinates. However, I suggest authors to provide more evidence that both perturbation methods produce consistent benefits for the unsupervised learning of the transformers.
+ The technical novelty of this paper is not up to the standard of ICLR. I believe that model performance is (marginally) improved but combining adversarial pretraining and positional embeddings is not appealing to me.
+ In addition, I wonder whether the proposed method can be applied to the supervised type in Table 1. Conceptually, the supervised objective enforces the model to learn meaningful features. The proposed method aims to do the same thing, and thus I wonder how well the model performs when the supervised objective is added.

Clarity: Clear.
Quality: High.
Novelty: Not novel.

Although the experimental results show some improvements from the proposed method, the technical novelty of this paper is not up to the standard of ICLR. In addition, the effectiveness of the proposed method should be verified on more commonly used datasets.

content.title: AdPE: Adversarial Positional Embeddings for Pretraining Vision Transformers via MAE+
content.TL;DR: We propose an Adversarial Positional Embedding (AdPE) approach for self-supervised learning.
content.abstract: Unsupervised learning of vision transformers seeks to pretrain an encoder via pretext tasks without labels. Among them is the Masked Image Modeling (MIM) aligned with pretraining of language transformers by predicting masked patches as a pretext task. A criterion in unsupervised pretraining is the pretext task needs to be sufficiently hard to prevent the transformer encoder from learning trivial low-level features not generalizable well to downstream tasks.  For this purpose, we propose an Adversarial Positional Embedding (AdPE) approach -- It distorts the local visual structures by perturbing the position encodings so that the learned transformer cannot simply use the locally correlated patches to predict the missing ones. We hypothesize that it forces the transformer encoder to learn more discriminative features in a global context with stronger generalizability to downstream tasks. We will consider both absolute and relative positional encodings, where adversarial positions can be imposed both in the embedding mode and the coordinate mode. We will also present a new MAE+ baseline that brings the performance of the MIM pretraining to a new level with the AdPE. The experiments demonstrate that our approach can improve the fine-tuning accuracy of MAE by $0.8\%$ and $0.4\%$ over 1600 epochs of pretraining ViT-B and ViT-L on Imagenet1K. For the transfer learning task, it outperforms the MAE with the ViT-B backbone by $2.6\%$ in mIoU on ADE20K, and by $3.2\%$ in AP$^{bbox}$ and $1.6\%$ in AP$^{mask}$ on COCO, respectively. These results are obtained with the AdPE being a pure MIM approach that does not use any extra models or external datasets for pretraining.
